candidate.name: Fly River
candidate.note: Natural river: the third-longest river on New Guinea (1,060 km), flowing mostly through Western Province. PNG Tourism names it as one of the two great rivers of the province; Wikivoyage describes river trips and charter boats from Daru and Kiunga. Pin is the Wikipedia infobox point (river mouth area), a long-feature point for the judge to review.

candidate.name: Fly River Delta
candidate.note: Natural area: maze of tidal channels, mangroves and inhabited islands at the Fly River mouth, reached by chartered boat from Daru (Wikivoyage). Near-duplicate of Fly River and Kiwai Island; listed separately because Wikivoyage names it as a visit. No coordinates found in OpenStreetMap or the sources; flagged for the owner.

candidate.name: Kiwai Island
candidate.note: Island: largest island in the Fly River delta (59 km long, about 4,500 people, villages including Iasa), reached by chartered boat from Daru. Wikivoyage names it as the delta's largest island; Wikipedia records stone axes used as grave markers.

candidate.name: Parama Island
candidate.note: Island: a village island 17 km east of Daru at the southern edge of the Fly delta, and the northernmost Torres Strait Island in PNG. No visitor source names it as a stop; added because the region brief names the PNG Torres Strait islands, so the judge is likely to reject.

candidate.name: Tonda Wildlife Management Area
candidate.note: Protected wetland: PNG's largest protected area, a Ramsar site on the Indonesian border with over 250 waterbird species and savanna wildlife. PNG Tourism lists 'Visit the Tonda Wildlife Management Area'; visits are based at Bensbach Wildlife Lodge.

candidate.name: Wawoi Falls
candidate.note: Waterfall in the middle Fly area of Western Province, which PNG Tourism names as a candidate for the province's largest waterfall. No Wikipedia article and no access information in the sources; location to be confirmed. No coordinates found in OpenStreetMap or the sources; flagged for the owner.

candidate.name: Hindenburg Wall
candidate.note: Natural landmark: a limestone cliff escarpment leading up to the Hindenburg Range in the North Fly District (Star Mountains). PNG Tourism names it as a sight; access must be arranged with customary landowners, and the cliff has been climbed and explored by speleologists. No Wikipedia article under this name. No coordinates found in OpenStreetMap or the sources; flagged for the owner.

candidate.name: Balimo
candidate.note: Town: centre of Gogodala culture in the south of Western Province, known for large decorated dugout canoes with 40 or more paddlers in races (Wikivoyage). Races are occasional events, so the town counts only as a cultural base; Balimo Airport serves it. Wikipedia title redirects to Balimo Urban LLG (the local government area), a broader article, so views are 0.
